before.physical_scope: Formulation definition inside the flat special-relativity framework: the Newtonian comparison momentum and kinetic energy are built from a named inertial frame, its spatial Euclidean structure, a positive mass parameter and a coordinate velocity, in the SI conventions of the framework. The definition asserts no approximation, correspondence or error bound, no Newtonian theory, no force or matter law, and no empirical content; the correspondence claim is pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence.
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $c>0$ with the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let $m>0$.

(a) For $w\in S$ define the *Newtonian comparison momentum* and the *Newtonian comparison kinetic energy* of the pair $(m,w)$ by $$N_p(m,w):=mw,\qquad N_K(m,w):=\tfrac12\,m\,|w|^2,$$ where $mw$ is the scalar multiple of $w$ by the real number $m$ ([[def-linear-map]]) and $|w|^2=\delta(w,w)$ ([[def-integer-power]]). With the SI conventions these carry the units kilogram metre per second and joule respectively.

(b) Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval ([[def-interval]]) and let $y:I\to A$ have inertial coordinate path $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$; writing $r(t)=r^1(t)e_1+r^2(t)e_2+r^3(t)e_3$ with real functions $r^1,r^2,r^3$, define the *coordinate velocity* $w(t)\in S$ of the path by $$w(t):=(r^1)'(t)\,e_1+(r^2)'(t)\,e_2+(r^3)'(t)\,e_3,$$ the componentwise derivative of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. The comparison functionals along the path are $t\mapsto N_p(m,w(t))$ and $t\mapsto N_K(m,w(t))$.

(c) The functionals $N_p$ and $N_K$ are comparison expressions built from a named inertial frame, the mass parameter $m$ and the path's coordinate velocity. They are not defined by, and do not presuppose, a separately developed Newtonian theory, and this definition asserts no approximation, correspondence, error bound or physical claim; those are the content of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]].
before.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: clause (a) applies the scalar multiple of a vector of the real vector space $V$ (restricted to $S\subseteq V$) and the square of the norm $|\cdot|$ supplied by the frame's spatial structure, both total on $S$; clause (b) uses the componentwise derivative of a function $I\to\mathbb R^3$ and the unique expansion of a vector of $S$ in the ordered basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]. No division occurs and no choice is used. The definition deliberately introduces no physical correspondence: it only names the two expressions that [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] compares with the model's measured quantities, and the units are the ones fixed by [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

before.title: The uniform second-order Taylor remainder of $z\mapsto(1-z)^{-1/2}$ on $[0,z_0]$
before.reference: scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08 ("Taylor with bounded second derivative"; constants depend on z_0); audit-expansion-report.md M08 branch
before.design_state: complete elementary argument from the published Lagrange-remainder supplier with an explicit uniform constant
before.statement:
Let $z_0\in[0,1)$ and define $f:(-\infty,1)\to\mathbb R$ by $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}=\bigl((1-z)^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1}$, the reciprocal of the nonnegative square root, with rational powers as in [[def-rational-power]]; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

(a) $f$ is differentiable on $(-\infty,1)$ with $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and twice differentiable there with $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; in particular $|f''(z)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ for every $z\in[0,z_0]$.

(b) For every $z\in[0,z_0]$ there is a real $R(z)$ with $$f(z)=1+\tfrac z2+R(z),\qquad |R(z)|\le K(z_0)\,z^2,$$ so $|f(z)-1|\le\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2$ for $z\in[0,z_0]$. Consequently, for every $\eta>0$, $$0\le z\le\frac{\eta}{\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0}\ \Longrightarrow\ |f(z)-1|\le\eta ;$$ the display is the quantitative form of $f(z)\to1$ as $z\to0^+$ used by [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]].

The lemma is a statement of real analysis about the single function $f$; it attaches no physical meaning to $z$ and makes no claim about a Lorentz factor or a physical velocity.
before.strategy:
(a) Write $f(z)=g(1-z)^{-1}$ with $g(y):=y^{1/2}$ for $y>0$, or directly apply the power rule: by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the rational powers of [[def-rational-power]] agree on rational exponents with the real powers differentiated in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], whose second clause gives $(x^{\alpha})'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$; the affine map $z\mapsto 1-z$ has derivative the constant $-1$ (identity and sum rules, [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]]), so the chain rule [[thm-chain-rule]] applied to $z\mapsto(1-z)^{-1/2}=y^{\alpha}\circ(1-z)$ with $\alpha=-1/2$ gives $f'(z)=-\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}\cdot(-1)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and repeating with $\alpha=-3/2$ gives $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; the identities $(1-z)^{\alpha}(1-z)^{-\alpha}=1$ and $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ are [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. For the bound: from $0\le z\le z_0$ we have $0<1-z_0\le1-z$, so $\tfrac12-$monotonicity in the base of [[lem-rational-power-monotone]] with $r=5/2$ gives $(1-z_0)^{5/2}\le(1-z)^{5/2}$ (equality exactly when $z=z_0$, by the strict part otherwise), and [[lem-of-inverse-positive]] gives $(1-z)^{-5/2}\le(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$; multiplying by $\tfrac34$ and reading $|f''|=f''$ (the strict positivity of the power, [[lem-rational-power-laws]] clause 1) gives the claim.

(b) Put $n=1$, $a=0$, $x=z\in[0,z_0]$ in [[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]]: $f$ has derivatives through order $2$ on the closed interval between $0$ and $z$ with endpoint continuity (indeed it is $C^{\infty}$ on the open neighbourhood $(-\infty,1)$ of that interval), and $|f''(t)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}=:M$ there by (a); hence $|R_{1,0}f(z)|\le M z^2/2!=K(z_0)z^2$ for $R(z):=R_{1,0}f(z)=f(z)-f(0)-f'(0)z=f(z)-1-\tfrac z2$. The final display follows from $|f(z)-1|\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)$ for $z\le z_0$ and the order arithmetic of $\mathbb R$ with the absolute-value properties of [[lem-of-abs-value]] ([[def-abs-value]]).

before.title: Uniform low-speed expansion of the observer energy, momentum and kinetic energy of a massive four-momentum
before.design_state: complete transport of the Taylor remainder through the mass-shell identities with uniform constants depending only on the speed bound
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, let $n\in V$ be future unit with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $U\in V$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$, $T_n(P)$ and $m(P)$ be the observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], and let $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=c\,h(U)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ be the Lorentz factor and relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d); then $u:=U/c$ satisfies $u=\gamma(n+w/c)$, $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ and $m(P)=m$.

Let $z_0\in[0,1)$, suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $f,R$ be as in [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]], so that $\gamma=f(z)$ and $\gamma=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$. Then:

(a) $E_n(P)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ and $T_n(P)=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ for the common real number $R_E:=mc^2R(z)$, and $$|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2=K(z_0)\,\frac{m|w|^4}{c^2},\qquad \Bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\Bigr|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,\tfrac12m|w|^2 .$$

(b) $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ with $R_q:=m(\gamma-1)w$, and $$|R_q|\le m|w|\Bigl(\frac z2+K(z_0)z^2\Bigr)\le\Bigl(\frac12+K(z_0)z_0\Bigr)z\,m|w| ;$$ moreover $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$ and $m(P)=m$.

(c) Every constant above depends only on $z_0$, so the estimates are uniform over all future unit $n$, all $m>0$ and all $P=mU$ with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$; if $z=0$ (equivalently $w=0$, $U=cn$) then $R_E=R_q=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$, $q_n(P)=0$ and $T_n(P)=0$. The lemma is a statement about the mathematical model only; it asserts no measured quantity, no approximation of a physical theory and no error estimate for any experiment.
before.strategy:
Combine [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) and [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]. Since $z=|w|^2/c^2$, clause (d) of the theorem gives $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}=(1-z)^{-1/2}=f(z)$, hence $\gamma-1=\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$.

(a) Multiply by $mc^2$: $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+mc^2R(z)$, because $mc^2\cdot\tfrac z2=\tfrac12mc^2z=\tfrac12m|w|^2$; and $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ by [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]\,(b), so the same remainder occurs. The bound $|mc^2R(z)|\le mc^2K(z_0)z^2=K(z_0)zm|w|^2$ gives the first display, and $2K(z_0)z\cdot\tfrac12m|w|^2=K(z_0)zm|w|^2$ gives the second.

(b) $q_n(P)=m\gamma w=mw+m(\gamma-1)w$, and $|m(\gamma-1)w|=m|\gamma-1|\,|w|$ by the product rule for absolute values ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]]); substituting $\gamma-1=\tfrac z2+R(z)$ and $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$ gives $|R_q|\le m|w|(\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2)\le m|w|z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)$ because $z\le z_0$ and $m|w|,K(z_0)\ge0$; the norm identity is clause (b) of the batch-8 lemma and $m(P)=m$ is [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]\,(b). The case $z=0$ is the vanishing of the remainders at the origin, $f(0)=1$.

(a) [Energy] $E_n(P)=mc^2+N_K(m,w)+R_E$ and $E_n(P)-T_n(P)=mc^2$; $|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2$. So the measured energy of the moving particle exceeds its rest energy by the Newtonian kinetic energy up to the displayed uniform bound of order $m|w|^4/c^2$.

(b) [Kinetic energy] $T_n(P)=N_K(m,w)+R_E$, hence $|T_n(P)-N_K(m,w)|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,N_K(m,w)$: the relative deviation from the Newtonian kinetic energy is at most $2K(z_0)z$.

before.physical_scope: Scope remark for the flat special-relativity massive-particle model and the same bounded low-speed domain as pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence: it records the failure of any speed-independent error constant as |w| -> c, the exclusion of ideal massless particles, and the bounded-region restriction of the Galilean chart limit. before.statement:
Scope remark on the limits of the low-speed bridge. Each quantitative assertion is an immediate consequence of the cited displayed identities; none of them is used as a premise elsewhere on this page.

(i) [No speed-independent error constant] Let $m>0$. For every $B\ge0$ there are a future unit $n\in V$, a vector $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and a state $P=mU$ whose relative velocity $w$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) satisfies $|w|<c$ and $\bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\bigr|>B$, with $T_n$ as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]. Explicitly, for every integer $\gamma\ge2$ there is such a state with Lorentz factor $\gamma$, namely $|w|=c\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}$, for which [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ while $\tfrac12m|w|^2=\tfrac12mc^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$, so $$T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2=mc^2\Bigl(\gamma-\tfrac32+\tfrac{1}{2\gamma^2}\Bigr)\to\infty\quad(\gamma\to\infty),$$ and the relative deviation from the Newtonian value equals $\frac{(2\gamma+1)(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}\to\infty$. Consequently the constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] necessarily depend on the speed bound $z_0$, no bound of that form is uniform on the whole domain $|w|<c$, and $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ and $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$ are unbounded as $|w|\to c$ although $\tfrac12m|w|^2\le\tfrac12mc^2$ there.

(ii) [The massless case is excluded, not a limit] An ideal massless particle of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] carries a nonzero future null four-momentum $P$ and, by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), satisfies $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$ exactly; it has no four-velocity, proper time or relative velocity, and no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy is assigned to it. More explicitly choose a canonical integer N>max(2,B/(mc²)+3/2) using thm-of-archimedean. The displayed absolute difference is greater than mc²(N−3/2)>B, and the relative ratio exceeds N−1.
